description: Verify ARP cache merge on two consecutive Requests from the same IP with different MACs — the second injection must overwrite the first, so DUT's UDP egress carries the second MAC (RFC 826 §2.3 'merge_flag')
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 826 §2.3 says the receiver updates an existing entry when a new ARP arrives for an already-cached IP. This case sends two Requests from the same sender_ip but different sender_macs and verifies that DUT's subsequent UDP egress uses the SECOND MAC, proving the merge actually happened.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request #1
   • sender_ip = HOST-1-IP, sender_mac = MAC-ADDR1

2. Tester → DUT: ARP Request #2
   • sender_ip = HOST-1-IP (same), sender_mac = MAC-ADDR2 (different)
   ⇒ DUT cache for HOST-1-IP must now hold MAC-ADDR2.

3. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup → DUT sends UDP to HOST-1-IP.

4. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: UDP with eth_dst == MAC-ADDR2 (the latest learned)   ← key check
   • DUT must NOT emit its own ARP Request (cache should be populated)

[Pass condition]
DUT's UDP egress carries MAC-ADDR2 as eth_dst.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_used_mac1 — eth_dst == MAC-ADDR1 → merge did not overwrite (kept first)
• Fail_unknown_mac — eth_dst was neither MAC-ADDR1 nor MAC-ADDR2 (corrupt cache)
• Fail_dut_arp_request — DUT emitted its own ARP Request → cache not populated at all
• Fail_timeout — no UDP within window

verdicts.Pass: DUT used MAC-ADDR2 (second learned) — merge worked
verdicts.Fail_used_mac1: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 — merge did not overwrite
verdicts.Fail_unknown_mac: DUT used some other MAC — cache state corrupt
verdicts.Fail_dut_arp_request: DUT re-resolved via its own Request — cache not populated
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit UDP within window
